record.title: The additive height conjecture for two pegs in peg solitaire
record.statement:
Let $A$ and $A'$ be points of a peg-solitaire board, and let $I$ be an initial position. Define $\operatorname{Height}(A,I)$ as the minimum number of legal moves needed to put a peg at $A$ starting with pegs on all points of $I$, with value $\infty$ if this is impossible. Define $\operatorname{Height}(A,A',I)$ analogously as the minimum number of legal moves needed to put pegs at both $A$ and $A'$, again with value $\infty$ if no such succession exists. **Additive height conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Height}(A,A',I)\ge\operatorname{Height}(A,I)+\operatorname{Height}(A',I).
$$

The claim would give a combined lower bound for the number of moves needed to place pegs at two specified points. The source presents it as a conjecture, and no resolution is supplied in the paper.
record.source_name: Olivier Ramaré, “A stronger model for peg solitaire, II”, arXiv:0801.0679 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0679

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2008).

record.title: Power-series identity relating the Leutwyler–Smilga series
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer, let $z_1,\ldots,z_N$ be complex variables, and define the Vandermonde determinant

$$
\Delta(a_1,\ldots,a_N) \equiv \prod_{1\leq i<j\leq N}(a_i-a_j).
$$

Define the power series

$$
\mathcal{J}_0 \equiv \sum_{k'_1,\ldots,k'_N=0}^\infty \frac{\Delta(k'_1,\ldots,k'_N)}{(k'_1!)^2\cdots(k'_N!)^2}z_1^{k'_1}\cdots z_N^{k'_N}
$$

and

$$
\mathcal{J}_m \equiv \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_N=0}^\infty \frac{\Delta(k_1,\ldots,k_m)\Delta(k_{m+1},\ldots,k_N)}{(k_1!)^2\cdots(k_N!)^2}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\prod_{j=m+1}^N\frac{z_i-z_j}{k_i+k_j+1}\right)z_1^{k_1}\cdots z_N^{k_N}.
$$

**Power-series identity conjecture.** The two series are identical:

$$
\mathcal{J}_0=\mathcal{J}_m
$$

for all $m$ with $1\leq m\leq N$. This identity is used to transform the character expansion of the Leutwyler–Smilga integral and is presented as an unproved conjecture in the paper; its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: C. Lehner, T. Wettig, T. Guhr and Y. Wei, “Character expansion method for supergroups and extended superversions of the Leutwyler-Smilga and Berezin-Karpelevich integrals”, arXiv:0801.1226 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.1226

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2008).

record.title: Non-closedness conjecture for symmetric tensors of bounded symmetric rank
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Y}_{r}$ be the set of symmetric tensors of symmetric rank at most $r$, and let $\overline{\mathcal{Y}}_{r}$ denote its closure. Let $R_{\mathsf{S}}$ be the maximum symmetric rank for order-$k$ symmetric tensors in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$. **Non-closedness conjecture.** Assume $k>2$ and $n\geq2$. Then

$$
\mathcal{Y}_{r} \neq \overline{\mathcal{Y}}_{r}
$$

for any $r$ such that $1<r<R_{\mathsf{S}}$. This strengthens the preceding propositions, which establish non-closedness when $R_{\mathsf{S}}<r$ or when $1<r\leq n$; the intermediate range $n<r<R_{\mathsf{S}}$ is conjectured to behave likewise.
record.source_name: Pierre Comon, Gene Golub, Lek-Heng Lim and Bernard Mourrain, “Symmetric tensors and symmetric tensor rank”, arXiv:0802.1681 (2008).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0802.1681

record.title: Conjecture on the number of segments of each depth
record.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a set of $n$ points in convex position. The **depth** of a segment is the minimum number of points that must be removed from $P$ so that the segment is not contained in the convex hull of the remaining points. Let $s_j(P)$ be the number of segments with depth $j$. **The segment-depth conjecture.** For $0\leq j\leq \lceil\tfrac{n}{4}\rceil-1$, one has

$$
s_j(P)\leq 3n-8j-6.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by a construction intended to attain the stated bound throughout the indicated range, and would imply a stronger abundance result for deep pairs in the planar circle problem. It remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Pedro Ramos and Raquel Viaña, “Depth of segments and circles through points enclosing many points: a note”, arXiv:0803.1088 (2008).

record.title: The conjecture that general-relativistic gravitation is effective quantum-states thermodynamics
record.statement: Let a General Relativistic spacetime determine a gravitational field, and let its associated quantum states admit an effective thermodynamic description. **Gravitational thermodynamics conjecture.** Gravitation determined by General Relativistic spacetime can be described as the effective quantum states thermodynamics. The paper presents this as a proposed bridge between pseudo-Riemannian spacetime, quantum states, and thermodynamics, but the supplied text gives no precise mathematical formulation or evidence of resolution.

record.title: Primes in irrational Beatty sequences
record.statement: Let $\alpha>0$ be an irrational number and let $\beta$ be a real number. The expression $\floor{\alpha p+\beta}$ denotes the largest integer not exceeding $\alpha p+\beta$. **Primes in irrational Beatty sequences conjecture.** There exist infinitely many primes $p$ such that $\floor{\alpha p+\beta}$ is also prime. This is motivated by the binary Goldbach and twin primes conjectures and concerns simultaneous primality along an irrational Beatty sequence. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Polynomial bound conjecture for unavoidable tournaments
record.statement:
Let $T(k,\epsilon)$ be the minimum positive integer such that every tournament $T$ with $n\geq T(k,\epsilon)$ vertices that is $\epsilon$-far from being transitive contains the tournament $D_k$. **Polynomial bound conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that

$$
T(k,\epsilon)\leq \epsilon^{-ck}.
$$

The paper presents this as a proposed improvement to the dependence on $\epsilon$ in the preceding theorem's bound. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture remains open in this record.
record.source_name: Jacob Fox and Benny Sudakov, “Unavoidable patterns”, arXiv:0803.2375 (2008).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.2375

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2008). “This conjecture was proved by Cutler and Mont\'agh, who showed that $n(k,\epsilon)<4^{k/\epsilon}$.”

record.title: The bounded-degree-3 four-edge decomposition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree at most $3$. A subgraph in the decomposition is counted at a vertex when the vertex belongs to it.

**Four-edge decomposition conjecture.** The edges of $G$ can be partitioned into subgraphs with at most $4$ edges, in such a way that each vertex belongs to at most $2$ subgraphs.

This conjecture would determine the remaining case of the traffic grooming parameter: together with the established bounds, it is equivalent to $M(4,3)=2$, whereas the paper shows only that $M(4,3)$ is either $2$ or $3$.

record.title: Conjecture on unbounded minimum cardinalities of maximal integral point sets
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\mathcal{A}_{q,s}$ denote the number of non-isomorphic inclusion-maximal integral point sets over $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ having cardinality $s$. Write $l_q$ for the minimum cardinality occurring among such sets.

**Unbounded-minimum conjecture.** For each $w\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists $q_w\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
l_q\ge w
$$

for $q\ge q_w$; equivalently,

$$
\mathcal{A}_{q,s}=0
$$

for $s<w$ and $q\ge q_w$.

This predicts that the minimum size of an inclusion-maximal integral point set tends to infinity with the field size, extending the paper's finite computational observations.
record.source_name: Michael Kiermaier and Sascha Kurz, “Maximal integral point sets in affine planes over finite fields”, arXiv:0804.1285 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.1285

record.title: Completeness of maximum integral point sets over prime-power residue rings
record.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and $r$ a positive integer. An **integral point set** in $\mathbb{Z}_{p^r}^2$ is a set of points whose pairwise squared distances are quadratic residues in $\mathbb{Z}_{p^r}$. Two such sets are considered isomorphic under the relevant affine isometries. **Completeness conjecture.** The above list is the complete list of maximum integral point sets in $\mathbb{Z}_{p^r}^2$ up to isomorphism. This asserts that the constructions listed in the surrounding discussion exhaust all maximum examples; no proof or resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Sascha Kurz, “Integral point sets over finite fields”, arXiv:0804.1289 (2008).

record.title: Exact value of the normalized integral-point-set number when $-1$ is a square
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, let $\square_q$ denote the set of squares in $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $\overline{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbb{F}_q,2)$ denote the normalized maximum size of an integral point set in the affine plane over $\mathbb{F}_q$. **Exact-value conjecture.** If $-1\in\square_q$, then

$$
\overline{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbb{F}_q,2)=\frac{q-1}{2}.
$$

The preceding corollary establishes only the bounds $\frac{q-1}{2}\le\overline{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbb{F}_q,2)\le\frac{q+3}{2}$ in this case, so the asserted equality sharpens the upper bound and is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The minimum oriented diameter bound in terms of vertex-cover number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless connected graph, and let $\gamma(G)$ denote its vertex-cover number. Define the minimum oriented diameter by

$$
\overset{\longrightarrow}{diam}_{min}(G)=\min\{diam(\overset{\rightarrow}{G}):\overset{\rightarrow}{G}\text{ is an orientation of }G\}.
$$

**Minimum oriented diameter conjecture.**

$$
\Xi(\gamma)=\left\lceil\frac{7\gamma(G)+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The paper proves the upper bound $\Xi(\gamma)\leq 4\gamma$ and presents the displayed formula as the expected true upper bound; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: LC-orbit minimum-degree conjecture for the interlace polynomial Q
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta$ be the minimum vertex degree among all graphs in the LC orbit of $G$. Suppose that there is no graph $G'$ on $n$ vertices with

$$
Q(G',4)<Q(G,4).
$$

**LC-orbit minimum-degree conjecture.** Then there is no graph on $n$ vertices whose minimum vertex degree among all graphs in its LC orbit is greater than $\delta$. The statement proposes a relation between minimizing $Q(G,4)$ and maximizing the minimum degree within a local-complementation orbit; the paper presents it as an open conjecture supported by the computational data in its tables.

record.title: The GLIN generation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, and let $\operatorname{GA}_n(k)$ be the group of polynomial automorphisms. If $\operatorname{char}(k)\ne2$, let $\operatorname{GLIN}_n(k)$ be the smallest normal subgroup of $\operatorname{GA}_n(k)$ containing the linearizable polynomial automorphisms.

**GLIN generation conjecture.** If $\operatorname{char}(k)\ne2$, then

$$
\operatorname{GLIN}_n(k)=\operatorname{GA}_n(k).
$$

The paper motivates this by the inclusion of tame automorphisms in $\operatorname{GLIN}_n(k)$ and the result that the Nagata automorphism belongs to $\operatorname{GLIN}_n(\mathbb{C})$. The conjecture is presented as new and no resolution is reported.

record.title: The conjecture that every divisible-order complete graph has a 3-symmetric optimal drawing
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph drawn geometrically, with vertices represented by points in general position and edges by straight-line segments. A drawing is **optimal** if it has the minimum possible number of crossings among geometric drawings of $K_n$, and it is **3-symmetric** if it has 3-fold symmetry.

**3-symmetric optimal-drawing conjecture.** For each positive integer $n$ divisible by $3$, there is an optimal geometric drawing of $K_n$ that is 3-symmetric.

The conjecture is suggested by the resemblance between known optimal constructions and 3-symmetric point sets, although the paper notes that previously known explicit best constructions were generally not 3-symmetric. The assertion remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on linearly normal Legendrian varieties
record.statement:
Let $V$ be a vector space and let $X\subset {\mathbb P}(V)$ be a smooth linearly normal Legendrian variety, where **linearly normal** means that the embedding is given by a complete linear system. A **subadjoint variety** is one of the standard Legendrian varieties associated with adjoint varieties.

**Conjecture on linearly normal Legendrian varieties.** $X$ is one of the subadjoint varieties.

This conjecture is posed as an open classification problem for smooth linearly normal Legendrian varieties. The source gives no resolution or partial classification sufficient to determine its status more precisely.

record.title: The minimum-semidegree conjecture for cycles of given length in oriented graphs
record.statement:
Let $ell
g eq 4$ be a positive integer, and let $k$ be the smallest integer greater than $2$ that does not divide $ell$. For an oriented graph $G$, write $delta^0(G)=\min\{\delta^+(G),\delta^-(G)\}$ for its minimum semidegree.

**Minimum-semidegree conjecture for $ell$-cycles.** There exists an integer $n_0=n_0(ell)$ such that every oriented graph $G$ on $n
g eq n_0$ vertices with

$$
\delta^0(G)\geq \left\lfloor\frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor+1
$$

contains an $ell$-cycle.

The conjecture proposes that the bound supplied by the blow-up of a $k$-cycle is asymptotically sharp for forcing an $ell$-cycle. The paper proves the corresponding bound when $ell$ is not divisible by $3$ and discusses the conjecture for the remaining lengths.
record.source_name: Luke Kelly, Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Cycles Of Given Length In Oriented Graphs”, arXiv:0806.0933 (2009).

record.title: The convex-dimension bound for poset poly-antimatroids
record.statement:
Let an **$n$-dimensional poset poly-antimatroid** be an $n$-dimensional poly-antimatroid that is closed under intersection, and let its **convex dimension** be the minimum number of chains whose unions describe the poly-antimatroid.

**Convex-dimension bound conjecture.** The convex dimension of an $n$-dimensional poset poly-antimatroid is at most $n$.

This would generalize the preceding three-dimensional consequence from the proposed staircase characterization. The source provides no resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: Non-recursive enumerability of the minimum equational graph theory
record.statement:
A **graph model** is a graph model of the $bb$-calculus, and its equational theory is denoted by $Th(\mathscr{M})$. The **minimum equational graph theory** is the least equational theory among graph models.

**Minimum-theory conjecture.** The minimum equational graph theory is non-r.e.

The paper states that it remains open whether the minimum equational graph theory is r.e.; this is the weakest of the listed open instances of the Scott-semantics conjecture.

record.title: Asymptotic n/6 domination conjecture for degree-six triangulations
record.statement:
A **triangulation** is a plane graph in which every face, including the outer face, is bounded by a triangle. A **dominating set** of a graph is a set containing every vertex or a neighbor of every vertex. **The n/6 domination conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that every $n$-vertex triangulation with maximum degree $6$ has a dominating set of size at most

$$
n/6+c.
$$

The paper presents this as a possible sharp strengthening of its proved $n/4$ bound for maximum-degree-six triangulations; its truth is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: The 3-connected stabilizer conjecture for universal partial fields
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a 3-connected matroid. A matroid is ${\mathbb{P}}_N$-representable when it has a representation over the universal partial field ${\mathbb{P}}_N$. The matroid $N$ is a **${\mathbb{P}}_N$-stabilizer** for a class of matroids when its representations determine representations of the matroids in that class up to the relevant equivalence. **3-connected stabilizer conjecture.** If $N$ is 3-connected, then $N$ is a ${\mathbb{P}}_N$-stabilizer for the class of ${\mathbb{P}}_N$-representable matroids.

The conjecture is presented as related to uniqueness of representation and as having important implications, including an immediate consequence of a theorem attributed to Geelen, Gerards, and Whittle. The source does not state that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: R. A. Pendavingh and S. H. M. van Zwam, “Confinement of matroid representations to subsets of partial fields”, arXiv:0806.4487 (2010).

record.title: The fixed-element settlement conjecture for representable matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a representable matroid and let $e$ be an element of $M$. The deletion $M{-} e$ **settles** $M$ when representations of $M{-} e$ determine representations of $M$ in the relevant sense, and $e$ is **fixed** in $M$ when its representation is forced by the remaining structure. **Fixed-element settlement conjecture.** $M{-} e$ settles $M$ if and only if $e$ is fixed in $M$.

The conjecture is motivated by the relationship between the Settlement Theorem and free expansions. The source does not provide a resolution.

record.title: Equivalences for the remaining MOY relations in graded matrix factorizations
record.statement:
Let ${\mathrm{HMF}}^{gr}$ be the category of graded matrix factorizations used to construct intertwiners of the fundamental representations of the quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$, and let the MOY relations denote the remaining local graphical relations in the associated calculus. **For Strategy (S1).** There are equivalences in the category ${\mathrm{HMF}}^{gr}$ corresponding to the remaining MOY relations.

These equivalences would complete the verification of the MOY relations for the matrix-factorization construction and thereby support the categorification of the corresponding quantum-group intertwiners. The source does not establish them here, so their status remains open.

record.title: Pink's conjecture on ordinary reduction of abelian varieties
record.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. A model $\mathcal{A}$ of $A$ over the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ of a number field $K$ satisfies **Hypothesis H** when there is a positive-density set of primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ at which the special fibre $\mathcal{A}_{\mathfrak{p}}$ has $p$-rank equal to $g=\dim A$. **Pink's conjecture.** There exist a field of definition $K$ for $A$ and an integral model $\mathcal{A}$ of $A$ over $\mathcal{O}_K$ satisfying Hypothesis H. This conjecture would remove the sole restriction needed for the paper's lower bounds for the essential minimum of subvarieties of abelian varieties, making those bounds unconditional; it is attributed in the source to Pink.

record.title: The 2-adic valuation conjecture for Stirling-number-related quantities at powers of two
record.statement:
Let $e_2(k,n)$, $\overline e_2(n)$, and $s_2(n)$ be the quantities defined in the paper, with

$$
\overline e_2(n):=\max\{e_2(k,n):k\in\mathbb Z\}.
$$

Here $\nu$ denotes the 2-adic valuation, with the convention $\nu(0)=\infty$.

**Power-of-two valuation conjecture.** If $n=2^t$, then

$$
\overline e_2(n)=e_2(n-1,n)=s_2(n)+1,
$$

while if $n=2^t+1$, then

$$
\overline e_2(n)=e_2(n-1,n)+1=s_2(n)+1.
$$

These identities predict the exact maximum of the relevant 2-adic valuations for the two families $n=2^t$ and $n=2^t+1$, and are motivated by the paper's analysis of divisibility properties of Stirling numbers. The paper describes an approach toward proving them; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Donald M Davis, “Divisibility by 2 and 3 of certain Stirling numbers”, arXiv:0807.2629 (2008).

record.title: List-colouring extension of Wegner's conjecture for nice graph families
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nice family of graphs, and let $G\in\mathcal{F}$ have maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ sufficiently large.

**List-colouring extension of Wegner's conjecture.**

$$
\chi(G^2)\le\mathit{ch}(G^2)\le\left\lfloor\frac32\,\Delta(G)\right\rfloor+1.
$$

The source notes that this is true for the family of $K_4$-minor-free graphs, by results of Lih, Wang and Zhu and of Hetherington and Woodall. The conjecture remains open for general nice families in the source.

record.title: Multipartite Hajnal–Szemerédi conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a balanced $q$-partite graph on $qn$ vertices, with vertex classes of size $n$. A **clique factor** is a collection of $n$ vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ covering all vertices of $G$. **Multipartite Hajnal–Szemerédi conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $K$ such that, if every vertex is adjacent to at least 
$$
{q-1 \over q}n+K
$$
 vertices in each of the other vertex classes, then $G$ contains a clique factor. This is the natural multipartite analogue of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem; the conjecture asks whether an additive constant suffices above the proportional minimum-degree threshold.
record.source_name: Bela Csaba, “Approximate Multipartite Version of the Hajnal–Szemerédi Theorem”, arXiv:0807.4463 (2008).

record.title: The DKSS conjecture on distinct products in finite abelian groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|>1$, and let $p(G)$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$. Let $k<p(G)$ be a positive integer. Assume that $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ is a $k$-subset of $G$ and that $b_1,\ldots,b_k$ are not necessarily distinct elements of $G$. **The DKSS conjecture.** There is a permutation $\pi\in S_k$ such that $a_1b_{\pi(1)},\ldots,a_kb_{\pi(k)}$ are distinct. The conjecture generalizes known results for cyclic groups of prime or prime-power order and elementary abelian groups; the paper proves it under an additional condition on the other prime divisors of $|G|$, but does not establish the full statement.
record.source_name: Tao Feng, Zhi-Wei Sun and Qing Xiang, “Exterior algebras and two conjectures on finite abelian groups”, arXiv:0808.2753 (2011).

record.title: The mod 4 characterization of continued fractions with $\mu(r)=-1$
record.statement:
Let $p$ be the parameter defining the family $H(p)$, and write a continued fraction as $r=[pk_1,2m_1,pk_2,2m_2,\dots,pk_{\ell+1}]$. Two such continued fractions are **(mod 4)-equivalent** if one can be transformed into the other by the five stated operations and their inverses. Let $\mu(r)$ be the associated invariant.

**Mod 4 characterization conjecture.** $\mu(r)=-1$ if and only if $r$ is (mod 4)-equivalent to either $[p]$ or $[3p]$.

This conjecture gives a classification of the continued fractions for which the invariant takes its smallest stated value. The source presents it as plausible on the basis of computations; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Generalized Grothendieck–Hodge conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety, and let $L\subset H^k(X,\mathbb{Q})$ be a sub-Hodge structure of coniveau $c$. The coniveau of a rational Hodge structure of weight $k$ is the smallest integer $c$ such that $L^{k-c,c}\not=0$. **Generalized Grothendieck–Hodge conjecture.** There exists a closed algebraic subset $Z\subset X$ of codimension $c$ such that $L$ vanishes under the restriction map

$$
H^k(X,\mathbb{Q})\rightarrow H^k(U,\mathbb{Q}),
$$

where $U:=X\setminus Z$. This conjecture relates the coniveau of a Hodge structure arising from geometry to support in codimension $c$; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

record.title: Monotonicity of the modes of shifted non-decreasing polynomials
record.statement:
Let ${\bf P}^m_\uparrow$ denote the class of polynomials of degree at most $m$ with nonnegative, non-decreasing coefficients. For $P\in{\bf P}^m_\uparrow$ and $d>0$, let $M_*(P,d)$ and $M^*(P,d)$ denote the smallest and largest modes, respectively, of the coefficient sequence of $P(x+d)$.

**Mode-monotonicity conjecture.** If $0<d_1<d_2$, then

$$
M_*(P,d_1) \ge M_*(P,d_2)
$$

and

$$
M^*(P,d_1) \ge M^*(P,d_2).
$$

The statement is proposed as an open problem after results describing the modes of shifted polynomials. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Yi Wang and Yeong-Nan Yeh, “Proof of a conjecture on unimodality”, arXiv:0809.1586 (2008).

record.title: Conjecture on gaps between generalized Hadwiger numbers
record.statement: Let $F,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be convex domains, and let $N(F,B)$ denote the set of generalized Hadwiger numbers associated with $F$ and $B$. For consecutive elements of $N(F,B)$, consider their distance. **Gap conjecture.** The largest distance between consecutive elements of $N(F,B)$ is at most $2^d$, with equality when $F=B$ is a parallelohedron. This would extend the corresponding two-dimensional result to higher dimensions; the structure of $N(F,B)$ and the existence of gaps are otherwise largely unknown.
record.source_name: Valentin Boju and Louis Funar, “Asymptotics of generalized Hadwiger numbers”, arXiv:0809.2490 (2008).

record.title: F-free hypergraph coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a $k$-graph. A $k$-graph is **$F$-free** if it contains no copy of $F$. Let $\Delta$ denote the maximum degree. **F-free coloring conjecture.** There is a constant $c_F$ depending only on $F$ such that every $F$-free $k$-graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most

$$
c_F\left(\frac{\Delta}{\log \Delta}\right)^{1/(k-1)}.
$$

This conjecture, posed in the earlier paper cited as [FM], proposes replacing the hypothesis of simplicity by the weaker hypothesis of being $F$-free; the source does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Alan Frieze and Dhruv Mubayi, “Coloring Simple Hypergraphs”, arXiv:0809.2979 (2008).

record.title: Conjecture on the maximal ideal and automorphism of the parafermion algebra
record.statement:
Let $V(k,0)$ be the universal affine vertex operator algebra for $
obreak\mathfrak{sl}_2$ at positive integer level $k$, let $N_0$ be its Heisenberg commutant, and let $\widetilde{\mathcal I}$ be the unique maximal ideal of $N_0$. Let $e,f$ be the raising and lowering generators, let $\1$ be the vacuum vector, and let $\theta$ be the automorphism under consideration. **The maximal-ideal and automorphism conjecture.** (1) The ideal $\widetilde{\mathcal I}$ is generated by the weight $k+1$ vector $f(0)^{k+1}e(-1)^{k+1}\1$. (2) The automorphism $\theta$ acts on this vector by the scalar $(-1)^{k+1}$. This would identify an explicit generator of the maximal ideal and determine its symmetry under $\theta$; the supplied text presents both properties as expected, with no resolution stated.

record.title: The property-(T) invariant-metric conjecture
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a group with property $(T)$ acting smoothly on a compact manifold $M$ and preserving volume. Let $d(\Gamma)$ be the smallest dimension in which $\Gamma$ has an infinite-image linear representation. **The invariant-metric conjecture.** If $\dim(M)<d(\Gamma)$, the action should preserve a smooth Riemannian metric. Measurable invariant metrics are known in several settings, but smoothness remains the conjectural step.
record.source_name: David Fisher, “Groups acting on manifolds: around the Zimmer program”, arXiv:0809.4849 (2008).

record.title: The three-small-triangles conjecture for five points
record.statement:
Call a triangle **small** if its area is at most $1/4$. Given five points in a triangle of unit area, consider the triangles determined by triples of the five points. **Three-small-triangles conjecture.** The five points determine at least three small triangles.

The claim would strengthen the preceding result, which guarantees only one small triangle. The source notes that three cannot be replaced by four for the displayed configuration; if true, the conjecture would imply corresponding lower bounds for larger point sets by averaging.
record.source_name: Matthew Kahle, “Points in a triangle forcing small triangles”, arXiv:0811.2449 (2008).

record.title: The Grassmannian Euler-characteristic conjecture for affine quivers
record.statement:
Let $Q$ be an affine quiver of affine type, let $
\lambda
displaystyle\in \mathbb P^1_0(Q)$, and let $E$ be a quasi-simple module in an exceptional tube. For a dimension vector $
\textbf v$, write $
\operatorname{Gr}_{\textbf v}(M)$ for the quiver Grassmannian of submodules of dimension vector $
\textbf v$, and $
\operatorname{Gr}_{\textbf v}^{E}(\operatorname{q.rad} M_E)$ for the corresponding restricted quiver Grassmannian. **The Grassmannian Euler-characteristic conjecture.** For every dimension vector $
\textbf v$,

$$
\chi(\operatorname{Gr}_{\textbf v}(M_E))=\chi(\operatorname{Gr}_{\textbf v}(M_\lambda))+\chi(\operatorname{Gr}_{\textbf v}^{E}(\operatorname{q.rad} M_E)).
$$

This identity is proposed as a way to establish the difference property and hence the generic-variable basis conjecture for affine cluster algebras; the source leaves it open.

record.title: Minimal transitive-subset conjecture for permutation encoding of input-symmetric degraded broadcast channels
record.statement:
Let $k$ be the alphabet size of the channel input, and let $l_s$ be the alphabet size of the code for User 2 in a permutation encoding approach. For an input-symmetric degraded broadcast channel, let $\mathcal{G}_{T_{YX},T_{ZX}}$ denote the relevant family of matrices, and let $\{G_1,\ldots,G_{l_s}\}$ be a smallest transitive subset of this family. **Minimal transitive-subset conjecture.** The code alphabet size satisfies $l_s=k$, and

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{l_s}G_j=\boldsymbol{1}\boldsymbol{1}^T.
$$

This conjecture concerns whether permutation encoding achieves the stated alphabet-size bound for User 2 on every input-symmetric degraded broadcast channel. The supplied text does not state whether the claim has been proved or disproved.

record.title: The convex-polygon realization conjecture for maximum rectilinear crossing numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be any graph. A rectilinear drawing represents the vertices of $G$ by points in the plane and its edges by straight-line segments. A **convex-polygon drawing** is one in which all vertices are vertex points of a convex polygon.

**Convex-polygon realization conjecture.** The maximum rectilinear crossing number of $G$ can be realized in a convex-polygon drawing.

If true, this would reduce the search for maximum rectilinear crossing numbers to drawings with all vertices in convex position. The paper presents this as a general conjecture useful for determining the maximum rectilinear crossing number.
record.source_name: Matthew Alpert, Elie Feder and Heiko Harborth, “The Maximum of the Maximum Rectilinear Crossing Numbers of d-regular Graphs of Order n”, arXiv:0812.1917 (2008).

record.title: All-orders Hamiltonian conjecture for rotational water waves
record.statement:
Let $\epsilon$ and $\delta$ be the perturbation parameters, and let $\mathcal{H}_{nm}$ denote the Hamiltonian contribution of bidegree $(n,m)$ in the grading with respect to $(\epsilon,\delta)$. **All-orders Hamiltonian conjecture.** The full system is Hamiltonian with respect to

$$
\mathcal{H}=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty}\bigoplus_{m=0}^{\infty}\mathcal{H}_{nm}.
$$

The preceding perturbative calculations exhibit Hamiltonian formulations through the displayed orders and suggest an infinite hierarchy of Hamiltonians, but the all-orders assertion is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Four-conjugate intersection conjecture for solvable Hall subgroups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $i]$ be a set of primes, and let $H$ be a solvable $i]$-Hall subgroup of $G$. Here $H^x=x^{-1}Hx$ denotes the conjugate of $H$ by $x$, and $O_{i]}(G)$ denotes the largest normal $i]$-subgroup of $G$.

**Four-conjugate intersection conjecture.** There exist elements $x,y,z,t\in G$ such that

$$
H\cap H^x\cap H^y\cap H^z\cap H^t=O_{i]}(G).
$$

The assertion concerns how few conjugates of a solvable Hall subgroup are needed for their intersection to reach the largest normal $i]$-subgroup. The supplied text does not indicate whether this assertion has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: E. P. Vdovin and V. I. Zenkov, “On the intersections of solvable Hall subgroups in finite groups”, arXiv:0812.3204 (2008).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the minimizer of the ground-state energy
record.statement:
Let $\lambda_0(\alpha)$ be the ground state energy of the operator defined in the paper, and let $\hat{\nu}$ be its minimum value. A minimizer is a point $\alpha_{\rm min}\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfying $\lambda_0(\alpha_{\rm min})=\hat{\nu}$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** There exists a unique $\alpha_{\rm min}\in\mathbb{R}$ such that

$$
\lambda_0(\alpha_{\rm min})=\hat{\nu}.
$$

The source presents this as an additional condition intended to yield a lower bound on the splitting between the two lowest eigenvalues of the magnetic Schrödinger operator. No resolution is stated.

record.title: Linearity of motivic Hirzebruch class transformations
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex algebraic variety. Consider a natural transformation

$$
T:K_0(\operatorname{VAR}/X)\to H_*^{BM}(X)\otimes\mathbb Q[y]
$$

without the normalization condition on smooth varieties. Let ${{td_y}_*}_i$ be the degree-$2i$ component of the motivic Hirzebruch class transformation. **Linearity conjecture.** Every such natural transformation is a linear combination

$$
T=\sum_{i\geq 0}r_i(y)\,{{td_y}_*}_i,
\qquad r_i(y)\in\mathbb Q[y].
$$

This conjecture would mean that the normalization condition used to construct the motivic characteristic class can essentially be dropped. It is motivated by corresponding classification theorems for Todd and MacPherson Chern class transformations, while the asserted classification in the motivic Hirzebruch setting remains open.
record.source_name: Shoji Yokura, “Motivic characteristic classes”, arXiv:0812.4584 (2009).

record.title: Local lattice-count identity for the Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma
record.statement:
Let $(a,b)$ be a strongly regular semisimple collection of invariants with $a_i,b_i\in\mathcal{O}_E^{\sigma=(-1)^i}$, allowing arbitrary $b_0\in\mathcal{O}_F$. Let $\Delta_{a,b}$ be the discriminant attached to these invariants, let $\eta_{E/F}$ be the quadratic character associated with $E/F$, and let $M^{\operatorname{loc}}_{i,a,b}$ and $N^{\operatorname{loc}}_{a,b}$ be the local lattice sets defined in the surrounding discussion. **Local lattice-count conjecture.** One has

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{\operatorname{val}_F(\Delta_{a,b})}\eta_{E/F}(\varpi)^i\#M^{\operatorname{loc}}_{i,a,b}=\#N^{\operatorname{loc}}_{a,b}.
$$

This identity is the lattice-count formulation of the relevant orbital-integral comparison: the preceding propositions identify the two orbital integrals with the lattice counts, so proving it yields the corresponding parts of the Jacquet–Rallis conjecture. The supplied text does not state whether this intermediate identity is separately resolved.
record.source_name: Zhiwei Yun, “The fundamental lemma of Jacquet-Rallis in positive characteristics”, arXiv:0901.0900 (2009).

record.title: Simple 3-graph multiplicity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a **simple 3-graph**, meaning that every two of its edges share at most one vertex. For a hypergraph $H$, let $m_k(H)$ denote the corresponding minimum number of edges in a $k$-color Ramsey-unavoidable host hypergraph, as in the paper.

**Simple 3-graph conjecture.** There exists a simple 3-graph $H$ for which

$$
m_k(H)=k^{3+o(1)}.
$$

This is the $r=3$ case of the proposed extension of the clique result to simple hypergraphs. The analogous assertion for $r\geq 4$ follows from recent unpublished results of Rödl–Schacht and the third author, while the case $r=3$ remains open.
record.source_name: Tom Bohman, Alan Frieze and Dhruv Mubayi, “Coloring H-free Hypergraphs”, arXiv:0901.2061 (2009).

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for invariants of unconstrained hidden Markov models
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{f}_{n,l}$ be the unconstrained hidden Markov model with $l$ hidden states and strings of length $n$, and let $d(n,l)$ denote the maximum degree of its invariants. **Monotonicity conjecture.** For $n\ge 2l$, the maximum degree does not increase as the string length grows: 

$$
\cdots\le d(n+1,l)\le d(n,l)\le d(n-1,l)\le\cdots\le d(2l,l).
$$

The conjecture concerns stabilization of invariant degrees for hidden Markov models. The supplied text notes that an ideal-theoretic analogue of a preceding lifting theorem would imply a related conjecture, but does not establish this degree monotonicity statement, so its resolution is left open here.
record.source_name: Alexander Schoenhuth, “Equations for hidden Markov models”, arXiv:0901.3749 (2009).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3749

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2009).

record.title: A mixed Bruhat chain conjecture for Littlewood–Richardson coefficients
record.statement: Let $v\le_k w$ be permutations, let $u(\lambda,k)$ be a Grassmannian permutation, and let $\Delta$ be a mixed Bruhat chain from the identity to $v$. A mixed Bruhat chain is a concatenation of maximal chains in possibly different $k$-Bruhat orders. For a chain $\Gamma$ in $k$-Bruhat order, write ${\rm jdt}_\Delta(\Gamma)$ for the jeu de taquin transformation defined by the growth-diagram rules. **Mixed Bruhat chain conjecture.** There is a mixed Bruhat chain $\Delta$ from the identity to $v$ such that the Littlewood–Richardson coefficient $c_{u(\lambda,k),v}^w$ equals the number of maximal chains $\Gamma$ in $k$-Bruhat order from $v$ to $w$ for which ${\rm jdt}_\Delta(\Gamma)$ is a particular, arbitrary maximal chain $\Gamma'$ in $k$-Bruhat order from the identity to $u(\lambda,k)$. This conjecture is presented as the natural generalization of the classical Littlewood–Richardson rule; the paper establishes the analogous assertion in specified Grassmannian and descent-restricted cases, while the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Cristian Lenart, “Growth Diagrams for the Schubert Multiplication”, arXiv:0901.4149 (2009).

record.title: Graded Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial ring with its usual grading, and let $M$ be a graded Cohen–Macaulay $S$-module of codimension $c$. If

$$
0\longrightarrow F_p\longrightarrow F_{p-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow 0
$$

is its graded minimal free resolution and $\beta_j(M):=\operatorname{rank}(F_j)$, then **Graded Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture.**

$$
\beta_j(M)\geq\binom{c}{j}
$$

for $j=0,\dots,c$. The conjecture asserts that the Koszul complex gives the smallest possible ranks for a minimal free resolution; it is commonly formulated for regular local rings, while this statement concerns the graded case. The general status is not established by the supplied source context.
record.source_name: Daniel Erman, “A special case of the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture”, arXiv:0902.0316 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.0316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2009).
